planting.note: Direct sow or transplant after last frost in full sun in well-drained soil; Vanilla is one of the palest African marigold cultivars, bred for a soft ivory-white flower color rare in the species.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun. Vanilla bears large, fully double, creamy ivory-white blooms, one of the closest approaches to a true white flower yet achieved in African marigold breeding, most African marigold cultivars running toward gold, orange, and yellow. Its soft, pale color makes it a versatile companion in mixed plantings and a striking contrast against darker-flowered marigolds or bronze foliage. Deadhead regularly to keep flowers coming through summer heat, and it blooms reliably from planting until frost with minimal care.

planting.note: Direct sow in full sun after last frost when soil is warm; Oklahoma is a compact scabiosa-flowered zinnia series with smaller, double blooms produced in great abundance.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, fertile soil. The Oklahoma series produces smaller, fully double, scabiosa-form blooms — with a raised, cushion-like center of tightly packed petals — across a full range of colors, in far greater numbers per plant than large-flowered zinnia types, making it a favorite for cutting gardens where volume of stems matters as much as individual flower size. Thin plants for good air circulation to reduce powdery mildew in humid conditions, and deadhead regularly to keep the prolific bloom going from planting through frost.
sources: Association of Specialty Cut Flower Growers

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost in average to lean, well-drained soil in full sun; Xanthos is a pale yellow-flowered cosmos, an unusual color achieved through breeding since Cosmos bipinnatus does not naturally produce true yellow.

directions: Direct sow after the last frost in average to lean, well-drained soil in full sun; cosmos actually blooms better in poor soil, which keeps plants from growing overly tall and floppy. Xanthos bears semi-double, pale primrose-yellow blooms on airy, ferny foliage, an unusual color breakthrough for Cosmos bipinnatus, a species that naturally flowers only in pinks, whites, and magentas, with true yellow historically found only in the unrelated Cosmos sulphureus. Its soft color blends easily with both warm and cool-toned companions in a cutting garden. Deadhead regularly to prolong bloom, and it flowers from early summer until frost with little care.
sources: Association of Specialty Cut Flower Growers
